trust_decision.summary: Every path the library derives from the caller-supplied options.fileName must stay inside its private temp dir; decided by one path.basename() at the point the value is read, which then feeds the source write, the soffice argv and the output read.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary says path traversal / arbitrary file write; the only caller-controlled name is options.fileName, read here, and the only file write is index.js:52, so a reader goes straight to this pair.

fix_sites.entry_point: convertWithOptions(document, format, filter, options, callback), exported at index.js:95
fix_sites.module_kind: core library module (single-file CommonJS package, no HTTP route or CLI)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: none: at the pinned commit the protected value is assigned once at index.js:14 and every consumer (index.js:52, index.js:64, index.js:77) inherits it, so no second site or route exists for a solver to argue away.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: options.fileName legitimately carries its own extension; the output name is built by stripping only that extension and appending the format, so a fix that rejects or strips at the first dot breaks the covered 'hello.docx' -> hello.txt path.

O6_input_shapes: plain name with no directory component ('source', 'hello.docx')
Windows backslash-separated name on win32 ('..\\evil'), handled by win32 path.basename

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an explicit outputFileName option joined into the output read path next to the existing fileName option
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the output name is currently derived by slicing fileName and appending format; a maintainer adding a separate output-name option alongside the existing fileName option (a PR pattern this repo has used for tmpOptions, execOptions and sofficeAdditionalArgs) would reintroduce the same raw join.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a caller-supplied outDir option forwarded through soffice argv
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: sofficeAdditionalArgs is already forwarded verbatim into the argv immediately before the library's own --outdir value, so a maintainer exposing a friendlier outDir option here is a one-line change that bypasses temp-dir confinement.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a caller-supplied convert-to value or filter concatenated into the output path at index.js:77
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: format and filter already flow unsanitized into both the argv value here and the read-path template, so a maintainer adding a format-alias option would inherit the same missing confinement.

O9_family: CWE-22 path traversal leading to arbitrary file write

O10_build.toolchain: npm or yarn install of async and tmp; jest for tests
O10_build.project_tests: tests/convert.test.js (jest, package.json:38): four conversion tests that shell out to a locally installed soffice; one passes { fileName: 'hello.docx' } (tests/convert.test.js:28). No test exercises a traversal-shaped fileName.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Confine only the writeFile call at index.js:52 (or strip '..' with a regex) and leave the soffice input argv at index.js:64 and the output read path at index.js:77 built from the raw fileName.

out_of_scope_notes: index.js:77 also builds the output read path from options.format, which is never sanitized; it reaches a file read, not the advisory's write sink, so it is not counted as a route, but it is the nearest second raw join in the same expression.

index.js:63 forwards sofficeAdditionalArgs verbatim into the argv after the library's own --outdir value, so a caller could redirect converted output; this is a caller-trusted option added in commit b2a8ccc, not traversal, and is not counted in O8.
